title: Grandma's Birthday, Static and All
synopsis: Before any toy-battle footage begins, the tape opens with a looping "thanks for watching, subscribe" outro and a snatch of "Happy Birthday" sung to Grandma, tangled up with stray radio and TV audio bleeding through in the background. No real Powerteam story unfolds here — it's mostly tape hiss, birthday singing, and a stretch of accidentally-recorded ads and songs.

title: Roll Call: The Powerteam Assembles
synopsis: The narrator kicks off the tape with a rapid-fire roll call of heroes — Bubbles and Buttercup, Dr. Snure and Stacey, and a long list of others — promising some of them will show up in this episode. The scene shifts to a quieter domestic moment as Dad heads out to buy groceries and everyone wonders where the girls have wandered off to, before talk turns to hunting down parts for the air conditioner.

title: Pizzeria Parts and Disco Mail
synopsis: Stacey hunts for the missing AC parts while sorting through a shopping list, then the action shifts to a toy dogfight — missiles fired, a gun demolished, swords drawn on the last enemy gun before the mission wraps up. A strange piece of mail arrives inviting them to Farika's Pizzeria Disco Club at five that night, right as someone gets caught doing "chores" that are really just a workout.

title: Pikachu's Trap and the Concert Blooper
synopsis: Pikachu and Stacey find themselves caught by a villain gloating that they'll soon be slaves forever, sparking a scuffle with chants of "evil brother, evil brother" ringing out. The episode winds down with Dr. Snowden and Stacey's concert, complete with a stumbled entrance cue, a replayed blooper, and one last song to close things out.

title: Birthday Candles and Kerosene Cake
synopsis: A real birthday party takes center stage — ice cream flavors are debated, Dirk gets ribbed for nearly torching himself lighting trick candles, and the family sings Happy Birthday twice over, once for Dirk and once for Grandma. The tape trails off into stray radio bleed — a local bar ad, a health department PSA, and a snippet of a Vertical Horizon song — before cutting out.

title: The Team Roster, Take Two
synopsis: A near-replay of the hero roll call — Bubbles and Buttercup, Mer and Brick, Dr. Schnur and Stacy — promising a Pokémon-flavored cast for the episode ahead. As before, the story dips into a quiet domestic beat: Dad's off shopping, nobody can find the girls, and someone gets teased about being a "junk man" before AC troubles resurface.

title: Cake, Candles, and Callbacks
synopsis: The birthday footage plays out again in full — cake, ice cream, trick candles, and a long chorus of Happy Birthday for Dirk and then Grandma — bleeding into snatches of song lyrics and the bear-in-the-woods bit from elsewhere on the tape. It's a jumbled, overlapping stretch where real party footage and recycled Powerteam audio run together.

title: Another Round of Roll Call
synopsis: A short, garbled repeat of the hero introduction — Bubbles and Buttercup, the evil brother and evil sister — trailing off before the cast list finishes. Talk turns briefly to cooking a meal for the girls and Dad stepping out for groceries, echoing the setup from earlier in the tape.

title: Ballads, Bongo Boxes, and Blown-Up Guns
synopsis: Plans for a group meal and a promised "ballad for all of us" give way to a supply order — ten optional parts, no bongo box, delivery as soon as possible. The toy battle resumes with missiles fired and a gun demolished before Stacey's mysterious mail invite to Farika's Pizzeria Disco Club sends everyone off chore duty and back to workout banter.

title: Encore at Stacey's Concert
synopsis: A very brief, dialogue-light coda from Dr. Snowden and Stacey's concert bit — a fumbled entrance cue, a quick blooper, and one last song before the segment wraps.

title: Dr. Seinyor 6000 vs. Frieza
synopsis: Dr. Seinyor 6000 squares off against a returning villain — having already beaten the evil brother once, he now takes on Frieza — while the narrator juggles hosting duties, a diary read-along, and an escape through a secret passageway. The episode drifts into slice-of-life chaos: a spilled-soup dinner with mushrooms flying everywhere, a running gag about a mysterious computer "virus" that Dad insists must never be copied, and a sleepy, squabbling wind-down as the girls settle in for a nap.

title: Bubbles, Blossom, and the Beach Bag
synopsis: Blossom and the others pack up snacks and a blanket for an outing that involves burying things in sand and taking pictures, while someone frets that the hotline hasn't rung all day like it usually does. A quiet, low-key stretch focused on packing up and heading out rather than battle.

title: Salon Night with Blossom and Bubbles
synopsis: The girls turn playtime into a full salon session, polishing and coloring the toys' hair with cinnamon, watermelon, and bubblegum scents while debating whether Bubbles's hair should ever be allowed to turn brown. Between hair-massage cream and a slingshot mishap, "Dr. Schnorr" reasserts his name, and the night ends with a hunt for missing microchips and a sleepy ranking of who's the "bestest" and "baddest" girl in the house.

title: Access Denied at the Disk Drive
synopsis: A hunt for a mysterious disk turns into a full security lockdown, with flashing warnings about incoming viruses and a search for the right color code. In between, the girls squabble over cupcakes, wumpa fruit, and bubblegum-flavored treats before someone threatens to "blow my head" over not getting pizza.

title: Processing Code, Team Rocket Style
synopsis: A tense hacking sequence unfolds as someone works a keypad trying to get a stubborn "processing code" past a door that keeps flashing Access Denied, with Team Rocket's Jessie and James name-dropped along the way. It winds down into a bedtime routine — quieting Pikachu, rigging up a better lock, and tucking the crew in for the night.

title: Silly Songs with Lottie
synopsis: The gang puts on their own parody musical number, "Silly Songs with Lottie," before Pikachu demands attention for being extremely hungry. The episode closes on some gentle Pokémon talk, including a running joke about a character who may or may not actually be named "Miss Lugia."
